result.scientific_strategy:
## 285f0407-8cc3-401d-bdcd-2af73de9a61c / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm, full-angle reach-and-hold distribution. PPO learned strong behavior: the baseline checkpoint-100352 reached 97.0% on the research panel and 98.0% on the task-reference panel, while the transferred full-radius experiment reached 98.0% and 98.5% respectively. These are development measurements, not the official assessment. Broader radius exposure corrected two earlier near-base failures. Focused negative-angle exposure produced a checkpoint with 97.5% on its research panel and 98.5% on the task-reference panel, but it did not change the protected failure set and later training regressed. Across the detailed evaluations, the remaining failures are concentrated at negative angles and either never enter tolerance or enter it only briefly, so the cause remains unresolved.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than training reward or the training success proxy, is the relevant progress signal (`research/evaluations/` and `research/results.jsonl`). Later unchanged training degraded or plateaued around the measured checkpoint, so more steps alone are not established as an improvement. Full-radius training produced the best observed task-reference result, but its selected checkpoint still failed at 9.9 cm/-122.9 degrees, 9.4 cm/-127.9 degrees, and 18.2 cm/-154.8 degrees. Focused angular exposure removed two failures from the experiment-3 research panel at checkpoint-35840, but the same three protected-panel failures persisted and the completed-budget checkpoint fell to 97.0% while adding positive-angle failures. Detailed research diagnostics show both geometric misses and repeated exits from the 1 cm band; they do not establish that either failure mode is causal. The current reward gives hold progress but no forfeiture when a hold is broken, making hold-exit shaping a plausible diagnostic lever without proving that it will correct failures that never reach tolerance. Development panels are not the official assessment, and repeated episode identities are not new coverage.

**Open questions:** Whether the residual negative-angle failures reflect control or hold stability rather than target exposure remains unresolved. It is also unknown whether the experiment-3 research-panel improvement at checkpoint-35840 is reproducible or transfers beyond that panel, whether a stronger penalty for breaking an in-progress hold changes the repeated-exit subset without damaging reach behavior, and whether any development-panel result transfers to the official 200-episode assessment.
